Patient: Mrs. A
Age: 66
Gender: Female
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
Mrs. A was admitted to the hospital for aphasia evaluation 27 months after onset. The patient had a mild right hemiparesis, right visual field defect, and a severe aphasia. During language testing sessions, she would frequently become frustrated and blocked out reiterating "I don't know." During clinical evaluations, her verbal behavior was replete with echolalic emissions, which increased when anxious and upset. Mrs. A showed significant improvement in language performance when evaluated by her husband.

Summary:
Mrs. A, a 66-year-old woman, was admitted to our hospital for an aphasia evaluation 27 months after suffering a stroke. The stroke resulted in two simultaneous hemorrhagic lesions that affected frontal and parietal areas in the left hemisphere and partially spared perisylvian language areas. Mrs. A had a severe non-fluent aphasia characterized by a markedly reduced spontaneous speech and almost nil auditory comprehension. She also had automatic echolalia, verbal perseverations, and ready-made expressions. Throughout language testing sessions, Mrs. A would become frustrated, blocking out and reiteratively saying "I don't know." Verbal behavior included echolalic emissions that markedly increased when anxious and upset. However, when language evaluation was performed by Mrs. A's husband, her performance improved significantly.
